Peas are a reward of early summer: freshly picked pods are sweet, but sugars soon turn to starch. Although long grown for canning, freezing and drying, home-grown peas taste best picked young and eaten or cooked at once.
edits.after: Peas are a reward of early summer: freshly picked pods are sweet, but sugars soon turn to starch. Although long grown for canning, freezing and drying, home-grown peas taste best picked young and eaten or cooked at once. The names round and wrinkled describe the dry seed in the packet. Round-seeded varieties are generally hardier, making them useful for early crops; wrinkled varieties are usually sweeter.

additionalVarieties.name: Meteor
additionalVarieties.text: A compact round-seeded pea for colder or exposed sites. Useful for early crops.

sourceNote: John requests a round-seeded variety and removal of the deep-bed instruction from Seed spacing. Add Meteor, already a rank-6 Round varieties entry, without replacing the existing five selections or changing master ranks. Its compact habit and suitability for cold/exposed sites come from the master; round seed and earliness are confirmed by current seed suppliers. Heights are omitted because suppliers differ from the master; no canonical measurements change. There are no pH or liming references in this working spread. Original page-2 copy, ten pest rows and artwork remain.
introductionNote: Alternative requested by John: retain six varieties (original five plus Meteor) and expand the introduction instead of adding Douce Provence and Norli. Hardiness and sweetness are from the canonical introduction; the dry-seed meaning is confirmed by Teagasc and the John Innes Centre. Existing eight-variety proofs remain available for comparison. John approved the six-variety fuller-introduction alternative on 7 November 2026.
